title: Executable domain knowledge: open-source precedents
method: Primary-source documentation review; no precedent engine was executed. Each source was accessed on its recorded date. Mutable documentation is not an archived artifact.

field_semantics.documented: Summaries of capabilities and ownership boundaries in cited primary sources, not observed runtime results.
field_semantics.roles: INFERRED functional classification: declarative, transformation, policy, orchestration, validation. These are not exclusive categories.
field_semantics.agent_consumption: DOCUMENTED only where native integration is explicit; otherwise INFERRED from a documented callable interface. null native_integration means not established by this review, not absent.
field_semantics.provenance: Separate artifact identity from decision records. A source URL, metadata or revision label does not alone authenticate origin or authority.
field_semantics.assessment: INFERRED limits and reuse implications; not exhaustive product-wide absence claims.
field_semantics.testing: Available test facilities or documented checks, not a claim of executed or passing tests. Application correctness remains separate.

verdict.label: INFERRED
verdict.closest_artifact: P01: versioned, tested OpenRewrite recipe library; Apache Camel Upgrade Recipes is a concrete domain-owned example
verdict.strongest_authority_counterexample: P07: independently managed OPA bundles, configured signature verification and decision logs, with external enforcement
verdict.strongest_operational_terminology_counte: P09: Kubernetes operator pattern explicitly captures human operational knowledge
verdict.remaining_hypothesis: A thin cross-engine composition and evidence contract may reduce integration costs or authority failures; compare it against native composition before introducing another package format.

precedents.representative: OpenRewrite recipe libraries and Apache Camel Upgrade Recipes

documented.knowledge: Version-specific dependency and source migrations composed from named recipes.
documented.ownership: Recipe authors own transformations; Apache Camel maintains its upgrade catalog independently of the OpenRewrite engine.
documented.packaging: JVM recipe libraries and YAML resources under META-INF/rewrite; Camel distributes Maven artifacts.
documented.versioning: Artifact releases and version-specific migration YAML; composed latest/LTS recipe paths. Engine, parser and classpath dependencies affect execution.
documented.testing: RewriteTest/RecipeSpec before-and-after and unchanged-source assertions; Camel tests multiple migration paths and publishes a test JAR.
documented.execution: Build-tool recipe execution invokes machine transformations without requiring LLM interpretation.
documented.scope_limit: Camel explicitly excludes Camel-Quarkus applications from this migration route.
documented.license_scope: Camel recipe repository is Apache-2.0. This does not classify every OpenRewrite recipe library or commercial distribution; current recipe-testing docs reference authenticated artifact access.

provenance.documented: Named recipes, versioned artifact coordinates and source repository history.
provenance.assessment: These identify implementations; a complete decision-to-input audit trail was not established by the reviewed sources.

assessment.authority: Recipe selection and permission to modify the repository belong to the caller/enforcement environment, not the artifact name.
assessment.reuse: Use native recipe libraries and tests; this is the nearest existing migration package abstraction.

precedents.representative: CodeQL query, library and model packs

documented.knowledge: Semantic analysis queries and framework/library models expressed as query libraries or YAML data extensions.
documented.ownership: GitHub/community own standard query sources; custom publishers own their packs; CLI ownership and licensing are separate.
documented.packaging: Scoped query/library/model packs with qlpack.yml, published and downloaded with CLI pack commands.
documented.versioning: Pack versions and dependency ranges; codeql-pack.lock.yml records exact dependencies; model packs specify extension target version ranges.
documented.testing: Repository documents query/library unit tests; test-bearing packs participate in dependency locking.
documented.execution: CLI evaluates queries and applies model extensions to analysis, not source-code rewrites.
documented.scope_limit: Model-pack support is documented as public preview with language-specific availability.
documented.license_scope: Standard query/library repository is MIT; README points to a separately licensed CLI and commercial licensing requirements for closed-source analysis.

agent_consumption.label: INFERRED
agent_consumption.interface: CodeQL CLI pack and analysis commands

provenance.documented: Pack scope/name/version, dependency lock and source query libraries.
provenance.assessment: Pack identity does not establish an immutable execution audit or permission to analyze a repository.

assessment.authority: A publisher can revise knowledge independently of the client; licensed engine use remains a separate condition.
assessment.reuse: Reuse query and model packs; a new analysis DSL would duplicate an existing packaging boundary.

documented.knowledge: Dependency ecosystem modules plus reusable update preferences such as grouping, ranges and schedules.
documented.ownership: Renovate maintains built-in modules and presets; organizations/repositories publish their own configuration separately.
documented.packaging: Managers, datasources, platform and versioning modules; shared JSON/JSONC/JSON5 presets composed with extends.
documented.versioning: Engine releases separate from repository presets, which can be pinned to Git tags; unpinned references use default branches.
documented.testing: renovate-config-validator is recommended for preset CI; documented relative-reference acceptance can differ between validator and runtime.
documented.execution: Renovate interprets modules/configuration to produce update PRs under configured scheduling and selection preferences.
documented.scope_limit: Repository ignorePresets and configuration affect what shared settings are used; npm-hosted presets are deprecated.
documented.license_scope: Comparison concerns repository-hosted configuration and documented modules, not a claim that every hosted service is open source.

agent_consumption.label: INFERRED
agent_consumption.interface: Invoke/configure Renovate through its normal automation interface

provenance.documented: Preset repository/tag references and debug visitedPresets identify resolved preset strings.
provenance.assessment: A mutable tag or configuration trace is not authenticated immutable decision lineage.

assessment.authority: Shareable preferences are not necessarily enforced organization policy when repository configuration can override or ignore them.
assessment.reuse: Reuse preset composition and ecosystem modules while retaining a separate mandatory-policy enforcement boundary.

documented.knowledge: Syntax, semantic and data-flow checks coupled to optional source edits.
documented.ownership: Analyzer authors define diagnostics and edits; compiler and host infrastructure have separate maintainers.
documented.packaging: Analyzer and code-fix assemblies; template includes NuGet package, VSIX and test projects.
documented.versioning: NuGet package releases and compiler API dependencies; documented target framework guidance is independent of source rules.
documented.testing: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing checks expected diagnostic IDs/locations, negative cases and resulting fixed source.
documented.execution: DiagnosticAnalyzer reports issues; CodeFixProvider registers executable edits for a host to offer/apply.
documented.scope_limit: The tutorial demonstrates additional semantic checks needed to prevent invalid fixes; a first working example is insufficient.
documented.license_scope: This is a compiler-extension precedent, not a claim that every third-party analyzer is OSS. SDK archive points to continued development in dotnet/roslyn.

agent_consumption.label: INFERRED
agent_consumption.interface: Compiler/host APIs for diagnostics and code actions

provenance.documented: Diagnostic IDs, descriptions and source locations; package identifies the implementation.
provenance.assessment: Diagnostic context does not automatically provide complete causal history or authorization.

assessment.authority: Host settings determine diagnostic enforcement and whether a fix is accepted.
assessment.reuse: Preserve the distinction between finding an issue and applying an edit; reuse packaged analyzers and fixtures.

precedents.representative: rustc suggestions consumed by rustfix and Cargo

documented.knowledge: Compiler/lint knowledge of source corrections and edition migrations; rustfix itself contains no compiler-specific logic.
documented.ownership: rustc and external lint authors produce suggestions; rustfix/Cargo maintainers implement suggestion consumption and application.
documented.packaging: rustfix library crate and built-in cargo fix command consuming compiler diagnostics.
documented.versioning: Cargo/Rust toolchain plus crate release; edition setting is changed separately from cargo fix --edition.
documented.testing: cargo fix runs cargo check; documentation requires project tests after edition migration. Archived rustfix repository includes tests and property-test regression artifacts.
documented.execution: Automatically applies compiler suggestions; remaining diagnostics are reported.
documented.scope_limit: Only compiled code is analyzed; inactive features/cfg require separate feature/target selections, and some migrations need manual changes.
documented.license_scope: Archived rustfix source is MIT OR Apache-2.0 and explicitly points to its current home in Cargo.

agent_consumption.label: INFERRED
agent_consumption.interface: Cargo CLI or rustfix library; JSON diagnostics available

provenance.documented: Compiler diagnostic output and explicit toolchain selection provide source and execution context.
provenance.assessment: Retain toolchain, configuration and source snapshot separately; no universal signed causal record is established.

assessment.authority: The applier does not own compiler knowledge; permission to edit is still granted by its execution environment.
assessment.reuse: This is a particularly clean existing knowledge-producer/client split; do not move compiler semantics into agent instructions.

precedents.representative: Community Edition engine, YAML rules and rule-defined fixes

documented.knowledge: Structural patterns, messages, severities and optional rule-defined source fixes.
documented.ownership: Rule authors define domain checks separately from CE engine and commercial platform maintainers.
documented.packaging: YAML rules supplied as local configuration or through a rule registry.
documented.versioning: min-version/max-version specify compatible engine versions; author-supplied rule metadata is extensible rather than a universal content version.
documented.testing: semgrep --test uses ruleid/ok annotations and .fixed expected files; TODO annotations are non-failing; rule validation is also available.
documented.execution: CLI scans sources and --autofix applies rule-defined replacements; README documents semgrep mcp.
documented.scope_limit: Rules outside engine min/max-version are skipped without a fatal error; some operators require proprietary engine functionality.
documented.license_scope: README identifies CE as LGPL-2.1 and distinguishes proprietary engine/rules/platform; registry contents must not be blanket-classified as OSS.

agent_consumption.label: DOCUMENTED
agent_consumption.native_integration: README documents MCP server integration in cli/src/semgrep/mcp

provenance.documented: Rule IDs/messages and author-provided metadata, including metadata in JSON output.
provenance.assessment: Metadata can explain origin but is not verified provenance or approval.

assessment.authority: A caller must distinguish skipped rules from successful validation; agent consumption does not enforce execution policy.
assessment.reuse: Reuse tested rule artifacts and existing agent interface; MCP access is not a new MEDP capability.

precedents.representative: OPA policy/data bundles and decision logging

documented.knowledge: Policy decisions over input and data, independent of application decision callers.
documented.ownership: Policy/data publishers own bundle namespaces; evaluator and external enforcement service are separate responsibilities.
documented.packaging: Tar bundles with Rego/data, manifest, optional Wasm and optional signatures; bundle distribution can be remote.
documented.versioning: Manifest revision, roots and Rego version; bundle updates can be independent of app deployment.
documented.testing: opa test supports test rules, mocks, coverage and structured output; opa eval and opa test do not verify signatures.
documented.execution: OPA evaluates policy and can emit decision logs; bundle-owned data/policy cannot be changed through ordinary REST writes.
documented.scope_limit: Signature checks depend on loading mode/configuration. Decision logs can be masked, dropped or rate-limited.
documented.license_scope: OPA policy management is the precedent; individual externally supplied bundles have their own ownership and distribution terms.

provenance.documented: Configured signed bundles plus decision IDs, inputs/results, paths, timestamps and bundle revisions in decision logs.
provenance.assessment: Revision labels are not content hashes; configurable logs are not an immutable audit store; signatures do not prove correctness.

assessment.authority: The enforcement point must honor decisions, protect evaluator configuration and withhold bypass credentials; an agent cannot be constrained merely by being told to query OPA.
assessment.reuse: Strongest counterexample to new authority/decision infrastructure claims; reuse policy-as-code rather than inventing a policy DSL.

precedents.representative: Terraform Plugin Framework and provider protocol

documented.knowledge: Provider-specific resource/data-source schemas, API translations and custom functions.
documented.ownership: Individual provider publishers maintain API-specific behavior; framework and Terraform core maintainers are separate.
documented.packaging: Plugin server binaries downloaded and managed by CLI, exposing provider protocol operations.
documented.versioning: Provider requirements, exact lock selections and package hashes; lockfile currently excludes remote module version selections.
documented.testing: Go acceptance tests execute real plan/apply/refresh/destroy; TF_ACC guards against accidental infrastructure costs and credentials are required.
documented.execution: Terraform core invokes plugins to manage resources and read external data.
documented.scope_limit: Lock verification is trust-on-first-use; optional signed checksum sets still require trust in the signing key.
documented.license_scope: Plugin Framework is MPL-2.0. Current Terraform core is BSL-1.1 with additional use grant/change license, not classified here as OSS. Each provider needs its own license review.

agent_consumption.label: INFERRED
agent_consumption.interface: Terraform CLI invoking providers; no standalone arbitrary RPC portability assumed

provenance.documented: Provider address/version and checksums; installation may report signed checksum key fingerprints.
provenance.assessment: Artifact integrity is not evidence of the reason or authorization for a resource change.

assessment.authority: Core coordinates planning/execution; provider logic is API-specific and effects are bounded by external credentials.
assessment.reuse: Reuse typed plugin contracts and native locks; a neutral interface does not make provider knowledge neutral.

documented.knowledge: Human operational expertise: desired-state reconciliation, upgrades, backup and recovery.
documented.ownership: Operator authors own reconciliation behavior; custom-resource users supply desired state; Kubernetes supplies the API/control-loop environment.
documented.packaging: CRDs with controller deployment and container image.
documented.versioning: Controller implementation and custom resource API are separate artifacts; reviewed pattern does not prescribe one universal release scheme.
documented.testing: envtest starts etcd/API server for controller tests; built-in controllers and kubelet are absent, limiting lifecycle assertions.
documented.execution: Controller observes resources and calls APIs to make reality match desired state.
documented.scope_limit: Pattern includes orchestration and ongoing control, not only passive knowledge distribution.
documented.license_scope: Kubernetes ecosystem pattern; each operator implementation has its own license, not implied by inclusion in the ecosystem.

agent_consumption.label: INFERRED
agent_consumption.interface: Kubernetes API or kubectl manipulating custom resources

provenance.documented: Resource identity and deployed controller/image identify desired state and implementation context.
provenance.assessment: The generic pattern does not mandate an immutable reasoning/provenance record; specific operators may provide more.

assessment.authority: Controller credentials, admission and deployment permissions require independent protection.
assessment.reuse: Operator is established terminology for executable operational expertise; distinguish its active orchestration from a passive domain package.

precedents.representative: JSON Schema 2020-12 and JSON Schema Test Suite

documented.knowledge: Constraints and annotations over structured instances, organized by dialect/vocabulary.
documented.ownership: Domain schema authors own constraints; specification community and independent validator authors own language/runtime behavior.
documented.packaging: JSON schema documents, references, meta-schemas and compound schema documents.
documented.versioning: Specification dialect/version is distinct from a particular domain schema's content revision.
documented.testing: Language-agnostic schema/data/valid test cases; test setup must align dialect, remote references and optional format validation.
documented.execution: Validator applies schema to data and produces validity/annotation output; recommended output schemas exist.
documented.scope_limit: Conformance suite documents behaviors it cannot express/test; format annotation and assertion are distinct vocabularies.
documented.license_scope: Test suite repository is MIT; validator implementation and domain-schema licensing are independent.

provenance.documented: Schema references/dialect and validation output identify the constraint context.
provenance.assessment: A schema identifier is not a cryptographic digest, signature or authorization; retain exact referenced content separately.

assessment.authority: Validation cannot by itself enforce external side effects or determine policy ownership.
assessment.reuse: Use an existing dialect plus conformance fixtures; cross-client agreement needs configuration and reference control, not just JSON-shaped fields.

documented.knowledge: Dependency declarations and exact selected dependency graph; build/test coordination.
documented.ownership: Package authors declare dependencies; Cargo owns resolution machinery; consumers review selected dependency changes.
documented.packaging: Cargo.toml manifest, Cargo.lock and dependency source packages.
documented.versioning: Broad manifest requirements versus exact lockfile package versions and Git revisions; cargo update changes selections, --locked rejects resolution changes.
documented.testing: cargo test compiles/runs unit, integration and documentation tests for selected targets.
documented.execution: Cargo resolves dependencies and builds/tests packages through CLI.
documented.scope_limit: Locking dependencies is distinct from fixing application behavior, toolchain/environment reproducibility and policy enforcement.
documented.license_scope: Cargo represents the family; package contents and dependency licenses are not implied by the package manager.

provenance.documented: Lockfile records exact dependency selections and Git source revisions for the documented example.
provenance.assessment: A mutable checked-in lock is inspectable identity, not trusted authorship or proof that the graph is safe.

assessment.authority: Consumer can update the lock; required approval must be enforced elsewhere.
assessment.reuse: Native identities and dependency locks already solve much of package composition; do not invent a competing package resolver without evidence.

documented.knowledge: Schema evolution steps and ordered migration paths from current database revision to target.
documented.ownership: Application authors own migration scripts/environment; Alembic and SQLAlchemy maintain engine/dialect behavior.
documented.packaging: Version scripts and migration environment maintained alongside application source; scripts implement upgrade and optional downgrade.
documented.versioning: revision/down_revision links order scripts; alembic_version records current database revision; engine release is independent.
documented.testing: alembic check reports pending autogenerated operations and can run in CI; it shares autogeneration's detection limits and is not a full migration correctness test.
documented.execution: CLI computes migration path and runs scripts; autogenerate proposes candidates from model/database comparison.
documented.scope_limit: Autogenerated migrations always require review; renames can appear as add/drop operations and need correction.
documented.license_scope: Alembic engine is MIT; application migration scripts have their own ownership/license.

provenance.documented: Revision IDs/parents, script history and database current version.
provenance.assessment: Revision identifiers do not authenticate script contents or prove data preservation; current version is not a complete audit log.

assessment.authority: Scripts remain editable and database credentials govern effects; a downgrade procedure need not restore lost data.
assessment.reuse: Reuse migration graphs and native execution; do not equate an encoded path with proof that a transition is safe.
